name: segmentTree
description: A segment tree stores aggregate values (sum, min, max) for array segments. The root covers the whole array; each node covers a segment; leaves are individual elements. Build: O(n). Query/Update: O(log n).
aim: Build a tree structure over an array that answers range queries (sum, min, max) and point updates in O(log n) time — much faster than O(n) for each operation on a raw array.
howItWorks: Build phase: recursively split array in half, compute aggregate at each node
Leaf nodes store original array values
Internal nodes store aggregate (e.g. sum) of their segment
Query: traverse only nodes overlapping the query range
Update: change leaf, propagate aggregate changes up the path

realWorld: Database range queries: sum/min/max over a column range
Geographic systems: range queries over spatial data
whenToUse: Repeated range queries AND updates on an array
When O(n) per query is too slow
Range sum, range min/max, range GCD problems
alternatives: Fenwick Tree (BIT): simpler for range sums only, O(n) space
Sparse Table: O(1) queries but O(n log n) build, no updates
